title: Rice with carrots, dark green vegetables, and tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of whole‑grain brown rice cooked with carrots, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach) and a tomato‑based sauce. The combination provides a balanced mix of complex carbohydrates, fiber, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll and high amounts of vitamin K.
Tomato sauce made from ripe tomatoes is a good source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
The dish can be easily adapted for vegetarian or vegan diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from whole rice and vegetables promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Rich source of vitamins
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots, vitamin K from greens, and vitamin C from tomatoes support immunity and skin health.

items.title: May reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: Complex carbs and plant antioxidants help regulate cholesterol levels and blood pressure.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene and lycopene contribute to protecting the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Slow‑release glucose from brown rice provides lasting satiety and stable energy levels.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to rice, experiencing skin rashes or digestive symptoms.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Dark green vegetables like spinach contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose a low‑salt version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side to meat, fish, or tofu. Fresh herbs (parsley, basil) can be added for aroma. For extra crunch, sprinkle with pumpkin seeds or toasted nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it can be stored for up to 2 months after cooling and placing in a freezer‑safe bag.
